## Background

Child Issues should be useful hierarchy context, not merely read-only references. A user must be able to select a Child Issue from Issue Detail even when that child is absent from the active Issue List View, such as a closed child while viewing Ready. Current Issue Detail selection is derived from the filtered visible list, so it clears when filtering excludes the selected Issue.

Triage: ready-for-agent

## What to build

Make Child Issue entries in Issue Detail selectable. Selecting one replaces Issue Detail with that Child Issue while preserving the active Issue List View. Decouple Issue Detail selection from search and Issue List View filtering: once selected, an Issue remains visible in Issue Detail as long as it exists in the Current Workspace's loaded All Issues. Clear the selection only when it disappears from All Issues or when the Current Workspace changes.

## Technical Approach

- Build on the Child Issue section established by bsm-nd7.1.
- Use semantic button/list markup and accessible names for Child Issue entries.
- Resolve the selected Issue from `allIssues`, not from the active filtered Issue List, while leaving the Issue List's own visible/selected-row behavior coherent.
- Preserve existing workspace-transition clearing behavior and add explicit all-Issues disappearance handling.

## Considerations

- Do not switch the active Issue List View or modify its search query when navigating a Child Issue.
- Do not introduce a second issue data source; Child Issues and selection both use the loaded structured data.
- Keep keyboard access and focus-visible styling equivalent to the existing Issue List controls.
- Ordering and hiding behavior are intentionally outside this task and may land independently in bsm-nd7.2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each rendered Child Issue is an accessible, keyboard-operable control.
- [ ] Selecting a Child Issue updates Issue Detail without changing the active Issue List View or search query.
- [ ] The selected Issue remains in Issue Detail when view/search filtering excludes it but it remains in `allIssues`.
- [ ] Selection clears when the Issue is absent from `allIssues` or the Current Workspace changes.
- [ ] Focused tests cover cross-view Child Issue navigation, search/view persistence, removal, and workspace transition behavior.

## Test Plan

- Extend state derivation tests for all-Issues-backed selection.
- Extend Issue Explorer component tests for click and keyboard Child Issue selection plus filtering behavior.
- Run the affected frontend test suite and Ultracite checks.

# Implementation Plan: bsm-nd7.3 — Navigate to Child Issues from Issue Detail

## Goal

Make Child Issue entries in Issue Detail selectable. Selecting a Child Issue
replaces Issue Detail with that Child Issue while preserving the active Issue
List View and search query. Decouple Issue Detail selection from the active
view and search filtering: once selected, an Issue remains visible in Issue
Detail as long as it exists in the Current Workspace's loaded `allIssues`.
Clear the selection only when the Issue disappears from `allIssues` or when
the Current Workspace changes.

Build on the Child Issue section established by bsm-nd7.1 and the priority /
date ordering and conditional visibility established by bsm-nd7.2. The
section flow, ordering, and empty-state behavior stay unchanged.

## Current code and constraints

- `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx` owns the selected Issue ID and renders the
  Issue Detail pane. `ChildIssueRow` is currently a `<li>` of three `<span>`
  elements (ID, status badge, title) and is read-only.
- `src/issues/issue-explorer-state.ts` derives `selectedIssue` from
  `visibleIssues` (the active view's collection after search filtering). That
  is exactly what causes the selected Issue to clear when the view or search
  filter hides it. `selectedIssueId` itself is held in `IssueExplorer` state
  and is cleared by an in-render effect when the ID is not in
  `visibleIssues`.
- `getChildIssues(allIssues, parentId)` already returns the selected Issue's
  children in the priority/created order from bsm-nd7.2 and is sourced from
  `allIssues`, not the active view.
- Workspace transition clearing is already handled at the App level: the
  `IssueExplorer` subtree is keyed by `workspaceKey`, which the
  `applyWorkspaceTransition` and `applyStartupIssueLoad` decisions advance
  on every commitSnapshot / clearSnapshot. The local `selectedIssueId`
  React state is therefore reset on workspace transitions automatically.
- The `IssueListViewId` we currently select on is unconstrained, so we do
  not bind selection to a single view.
- ADR-0002 and ADR-0003 require Beadwork to remain the source of truth and
  prohibit parsing human-readable `bw show` output or adding another CLI
  call. This plan must not introduce a second Issue data source.

## Domain and repository constraints

- A Child Issue is an Issue whose Beadwork `parent` field exactly matches
  the selected Issue ID. The relationship is derived from the Current
  Workspace's loaded `allIssues`; it is not a durable field on the Issue.
- The selected Issue is resolved from `allIssues`, not from the active
  view's visible list. The active Issue List View's own visible /
  selected-row behavior must remain coherent: the `aria-current` indicator
  on a row still depends on whether the row is in the visible list, but
  the existence of the selected Issue in Issue Detail is independent of
  the visible list.
- Selection clearing has two triggers: the selected Issue ID is absent
  from `allIssues`, or the Current Workspace changes. The latter is
  already handled by the App-level remount key; this plan only adds the
  former.
- No new RPC bindings, no new `bw` command, no parsing of `bw show`
  output, no separate CLI call. Reuse `toIssueViewModel` and the existing
  badge tone mapping for entry presentation.
- A Child Issue entry is a focused, keyboard-operable button. It uses
  semantic `<button>` markup inside the existing `<li>` so the list
  semantics are preserved, and has an accessible name that combines ID,
  title, and humanized status so screen readers announce the same
  information sighted users see.

## Dependency graph

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Resolve selectedIssue from allIssues] --> B[Update clearing effect]
    A --> C[Reconcile cross-collection test]
    B --> D[Wire Child Issue button -> onSelect]
    D --> E[Add cross-view navigation tests]
    D --> F[Add persistence tests]
    E --> G[Run focused tests and checks]
    F --> G
    C --> G
```

## Implementation steps

### 1. Resolve selected Issue from `allIssues` instead of `visibleIssues`

Update `src/issues/issue-explorer-state.ts`.

- Change the `selectedIssue` derivation so it looks up the issue in
  `issueState.allIssues` whenever the load state is successful and
  `selectedIssueId` is non-null. The contract becomes: selection survives
  view and search filtering as long as the Issue is in `allIssues`.
- Do not change the `visibleIssues`, `baseVisibleIssues`, `emptyReason`,
  `hasSearchQuery`, `isSearchDisabled`, `activeViewId`, or
  `activeViewLabel` outputs. The active view's filtering is unchanged.
- Do not gate selection on `visibleIssues`. The selected Issue need not
  be in the active view's base collection or its search-filtered result.
- The lookup must remain an exact `id === selectedIssueId` comparison;
  do not introduce a fuzzy or whitespace-tolerant match.
- When the load state is not successful, `selectedIssue` is still `null`.
  When `selectedIssueId` is `null`, `selectedIssue` is still `null`.

### 2. Update the clearing effect in `IssueExplorer`

Update `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`.

- The current in-render effect clears `selectedIssueId` when it is not in
  `visibleIssues`. Change this to clear when the ID is not in
  `issueState.allIssues` (only meaningful when the load state is
  successful). This is the "all-Issues disappearance" clearing.
- Preserve the existing "do not auto-restore" semantics: a cleared
  selection is not re-applied when a later view or search change would
  make the Issue visible again. The auto-restore test will become
  invalid once selection persists across filters; replace it with tests
  that selection simply persists.
- Workspace transition clearing remains untouched — it is handled by the
  App-level `workspaceKey` remount that drops the `IssueExplorer` React
  subtree. Do not add a second explicit workspace-change effect inside
  `IssueExplorer`; doing so would double-handle the already-clearing
  state and risk races.

### 3. Convert `ChildIssueRow` into a keyboard-operable button

Update `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`.

- Convert the row from a `<li>` of three `<span>` elements into a `<li>`
  containing a single `<button type="button">`. The button is the
  interactive surface; the `<li>` and the parent `<ul aria-label="Child
  Issues">` preserve the list semantics.
- The button must:
  - render the ID, status badge, and title in the same DOM / visual order
    as the bsm-nd7.1 + bsm-nd7.2 contract;
  - call the existing `handleSelect(issueId)` handler when clicked;
  - carry an `aria-label` of the form
    `"<id>: <title>. <humanized status>"` so it matches the Issue List
    row's accessible name pattern;
  - have focus-visible styling equivalent to the Issue List row button
    (`hover:bg-white/5 focus:bg-white/5 focus:outline-none` plus a
    `cursor-pointer` and `text-left` since the visible content is
    left-aligned);
  - use a `key` on the `<li>` based on the child Issue ID so React
    reconciliation is stable.
- Reuse `toIssueViewModel(issue, issueMap)` and
  `TONE_BADGE_CLASSES[view.badgeTone]` for status presentation. Do not
  duplicate the status-label or badge mapping.
- Do not introduce additional metadata (priority, type, labels) on the
  Child Issue button. The DOM contract is ID, status, title in that
  order, unchanged from bsm-nd7.1 / bsm-nd7.2.

### 4. Thread `onSelect` through to the button

Update `src/issues/IssueExplorer.tsx`.

- Add `onSelect: (issueId: string) => void` to `ChildIssueRow`,
  `ChildIssuesSection`, `IssueDetailContent`, and `IssueDetailPane`.
- Pass the existing `handleSelect` from `IssueExplorer` into the
  `IssueDetailPane` and onward. The handler is already correct: it only
  updates `selectedIssueId`, leaving the active Issue List View and
  search query alone.
- Do not introduce a second selection state. The Child Issue button
  uses the same `selectedIssueId` state as the Issue List rows; clicking
  a Child Issue is the same operation as clicking an Issue List row
  from the user's perspective.

### 5. Update pure derivation tests

Update `src/issues/issue-explorer-state.test.ts`.

- Replace the existing
  "selects an issue only when it is present in the visible collection"
  test with cases that exercise the new contract:
  - selection resolves from `allIssues` when the Issue is in the source
    collection but not in the active view's base visible list (e.g., an
    open Issue selected while viewing Closed);
  - selection resolves from `allIssues` when the Issue is in the source
    collection but a search query hides it from `visibleIssues`;
  - `selectedIssue` is `null` when the load state is not successful;
  - `selectedIssue` is `null` when `selectedIssueId` is `null`;
  - `selectedIssue` is `null` when `selectedIssueId` does not match any
    `allIssues` entry;
  - `visibleIssues` and all other derived fields are unchanged across
    the contract change.
- The existing tests that assert selection clearing on view change or
  search query no longer apply to the new contract. Remove them and
  replace them with the persistence tests below.

### 6. Update the existing cross-view Child Issue test

Update `src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx`.

- The "renders the detail pane from the active visible Issue collection
  when the selected Issue spans multiple views" test contradicts the new
  contract. Replace its post-switch assertions with the new behavior:
  the selected Issue's detail is sourced from `allIssues`, not from the
  active view's command-backed collection. The row indicator on the
  visible row still updates because the row is in the visible list, but
  the detail contents come from `allIssues`.

### 7. Extend the existing Child Issues section tests

Update `src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx`.

- Remove the read-only assertions in the existing "renders matching
  children in priority/created order with id, status, then title" test:
  ```
  expect(section.queryByRole("link")).toBeNull();
  expect(section.queryByRole("button")).toBeNull();
  ```
  Replace them with a positive assertion that each entry is a button
  with the expected accessible name and the established ID / status /
  title display order.
- Add a `getChildIssueRowButton(issue)` helper alongside the existing
  `getRowButton` helper, scoped to the Child Issues section, so the new
  tests can target Child Issue rows without reaching into the Issue
  List.

### 8. Add cross-view Child Issue navigation tests

Add focused component tests in `src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx`.

Cover:

- clicking a Child Issue button updates Issue Detail to the Child Issue
  (title, ID, status all reflect the child; the previous parent's
  detail is gone);
- clicking a Child Issue does not change the active Issue List View: the
  `data-active-issue-list-view-id` attribute on the Issue List section
  remains at the value set before the click;
- clicking a Child Issue does not change the search query: the
  `<input type="text">`'s value remains at the value set before the
  click (initially empty, or whatever the user typed earlier);
- keyboard activation works: focusing a Child Issue button and pressing
  Enter (or Space) updates Issue Detail; the existing `userEvent` API
  covers both `click` and `keyboard` interactions;
- Child Issue navigation works across a forced re-render with a
  different `activeIssueListViewId` and a fresh load state — the
  selected child stays selected.

### 9. Add selection persistence tests

Add focused component tests in `src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx`.

Cover:

- selecting an Issue, then applying a search query that hides it from
  the visible list, leaves the Issue Detail unchanged;
- selecting an Issue, then switching to a view that excludes it, leaves
  the Issue Detail unchanged and the new view's empty / populated
  state intact;
- clearing the hidden search query does not transition the detail pane
  through the empty state — the detail continues to show the previously
  selected Issue;
- switching back to a view that includes the Issue does not change the
  detail pane;
- the active Issue List View's `aria-current` indicator on the Issue
  List row is set correctly when the selected Issue is in the visible
  list and is absent (no row attribute change) when the selected Issue
  is not in the visible list;
- the search input retains its value through the view-change and
  search-change scenarios above.

### 10. Add removal and workspace transition tests

Add focused component tests in `src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx`
and rely on existing App-level coverage for workspace transitions.

Cover:

- when the selected Issue is removed from `allIssues` (a re-render with
  a new load state that omits the previously selected Issue), the
  Issue Detail transitions to the empty "No issue selected" state;
- the previous selection is not auto-restored when the Issue reappears
  in `allIssues` on a later load (the cleared selection is sticky);
- workspace transition clearing is exercised at the App level. The
  existing `wdio.issue-list.conf.ts` + `App.workspace-switching.test.tsx`
  coverage proves that a workspace change remounts the Issue Explorer
  subtree and drops the local `selectedIssueId` state. Do not duplicate
  this assertion at the `IssueExplorer` level; instead, add a brief
  test that a `key` change on the `IssueExplorer` subtree drops the
  local selection (this is the React mechanism that the App-level
  tests rely on).

### 11. Validate

Run from the repository root:

```bash
pnpm test -- src/issues/issue-hierarchy.test.ts \
            src/issues/issue-explorer-state.test.ts \
            src/issues/IssueExplorer.test.tsx
pnpm check
pnpm build
```

If the focused changes require a full TypeScript / Vite build
verification, run the `pnpm build` target. Otherwise confirm the
TypeScript pass through the existing CI-equivalent check.

Review the final diff to confirm:

- no changes to `src/rpc/bindings.ts`, Rust RPC types, or `bw`
  invocation;
- no parsing of human-readable `bw show` output;
- no new RPC or CLI call;
- no Child Issue ordering or empty-state changes (those landed in
  bsm-nd7.2);
- no second Issue data source.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] `selectedIssue` is derived from `allIssues`, not from the
      active view's `visibleIssues`.
- [ ] The clearing effect in `IssueExplorer` clears `selectedIssueId`
      only when the ID is absent from `allIssues` (load state is
      successful).
- [ ] Workspace transition clearing remains handled by the App-level
      remount key; no duplicate effect is added.
- [ ] Each Child Issue entry is a `<button>` inside a `<li>` inside a
      `<ul>` with semantic accessible names.
- [ ] The Child Issue button shows ID, status badge, and title in that
      order using the existing badge tone mapping.
- [ ] Clicking a Child Issue updates Issue Detail to the Child Issue.
- [ ] Clicking a Child Issue does not change the active Issue List View
      or the search query.
- [ ] Keyboard activation (Enter / Space) on a Child Issue button
      updates Issue Detail.
- [ ] The selected Issue remains in Issue Detail when a view change
      hides it from the visible list.
- [ ] The selected Issue remains in Issue Detail when a search query
      hides it from the visible list.
- [ ] The selected Issue clears when removed from `allIssues`.
- [ ] The cleared selection is not auto-restored when the Issue
      reappears in `allIssues` later.
- [ ] Pure derivation tests cover the new contract and the
      previously-tested invariants still hold.
- [ ] Component tests cover cross-view Child Issue navigation, search
      / view persistence, removal, and workspace transition behavior.
- [ ] Focused tests, Ultracite checks, and the TypeScript / Vite build
      pass.

## Non-goals and follow-up boundaries

- Do not change Child Issue ordering or empty-state visibility; those
  landed in bsm-nd7.2.
- Do not add a `children` field to the Issue / RPC contract or a
  durable Beadsmith hierarchy model.
- Do not issue a new `bw` command or parse `bw show` output.
- Do not introduce a second Issue data source; selection and Child
  Issue derivation both use the loaded `allIssues` data.
- Do not add filter-aware selection semantics; the selected Issue is
  always drawn from `allIssues`, independent of the active view or
  search.
- Do not add a workspace-change clearing effect inside `IssueExplorer`;
  the App-level remount key already handles it.
- Do not add real-desktop WebDriver coverage; that is bsm-nd7.4.
- Do not add deep linking or browsing history; that is bsm-wz5.

title: Navigate to Child Issues from Issue Detail
